a.text: A mind as still as water.
'Tis a rare trait for someone of thy age.
Thou hast extinguished all light and purged all emotions from thy mind, and thus are all creations of nature leaving thy body.
At long last, the still waters in thy mind give rise to new emotions—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Master storyteller! Pray forgive my interruption!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Awake from your dream at long last... How long has it been?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I have seen the plums blossom and wither ten times.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: As long as my ink brush remain untouched, the scenery in the painting would never change.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: To tell the truth, I had been counting ever since the moment I entered the painting scroll of Mount Sky. 'Twas indeed that long.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: ...Ten years?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You stayed in the painting for ten years?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: More or less.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You, a mere wandering monk, fiddled away ten full years here. What drove you to partake in such meaningless tribulations?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Well, I could enjoy a good sleep, partake in all manner of indulgences, and I need not be disturbed by the world, to say nothing of the Catastrophes and infections. I thought it a rather pleasant experience.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Be that as it may, you dreamt... for ten full years.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Few are capable of remembering who they truly are after such a long time. Some would forget who they once were and choose to forever remain inside the painting.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: My, how frightening.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Yet you are not afraid at all.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: You are a kind man. I verily believe you would wake them before they cross that point of no return.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Oh? What makes you say that?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: The old fisher at the summit of Mount Sky, the weaver by the banks of the Pu-kuei River, the halberd wielder of the Wu-chieh Plains, the lady innkeeper of the Lungmen Inn... and now the storyteller of the P'o-shan Village... Thou hast reminded me countless of times.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Yet I chose to deceive myself and continued to indulge in my pleasures, never to wake from my dream. I suppose I must apologize. It must have been tedious to keep me alive in the painting.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Pray be at ease. You came to the mountain when the autumn winds were yet blowing. 'Tis merely the beginning of winter now. It was but a brief dream.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Hoh! I was worried I would be reprimanded for my sluggish behavior. Little did I know it was but a brief period of time. That certainly puts me at ease.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You already knew of your predicament when you reached Mount Sky, that it was merely a painting. Why waste your time?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: For I saw the truth of Dusk Beauty Flying to the Moon, and I could not well cease thinking about it... A madwoman took matters into her hands and sought to reclaim her true love from the heavens. 'Tis an act of pure lunacy, yet it overwhelms me with a sense of regret...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hmm... What if I tell you Dusk Beauty's willpower was an addition I made to the painting—that it is of my own making?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: All the nations of this world possess a great many legends, classics, literature, and myths, many of which can be called fabricated. The common folk are not likely to ever experience the machinations written therein. Should we disregard their lessons because they are mere fiction?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I think 'tis absurd to do so.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You are a strange one.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: There is but a fine line between great and strange. I appreciate your compliment.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You are just like your master. He's old, yet he has the heart of a child, a clear mind.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You've helped me pass the time... Out of respect for your master, very well, I shall grant you an audience with me.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Um, an audience?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Haha, you cannot possibly believe you've awakened by waltzing in here?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: *gasp*...! Am I yet within the painting?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: No need to feel ashamed. This is merely how it's meant to be.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If I let you break out merely because you wished so, it would blemish my image.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Well, now.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Wake up—

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Finally awake?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Get up now. It's terrible manners to sleep on the ground.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oh...! You are right...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Well... 'Tis merely that I never imagined you... to look like this.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Well, ask away.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I thought that by surveying the sceneries of these hundred-and-some scrolls, I, too, could walk the journey that thou once walked. Yet... 'Twas but an insignificant fraction of the landscapes thou hast sketched...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Know that there are those who never accept their mistakes and find themselves content with dying here.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: That I can understand...

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: That's not what you wanted to ask.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oh, right, I was startled into forgetfulness. My apologies.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Master, I have once laid my eyes upon the 'Scene of Crude Mounts Utmost Risen' at my head priest's garret. Though at the time I thought there was meaning hidden therein, I could not quite put my finger on it.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I asked the head priest, and he had me leave the monastery to seek out the answer. I have since traveled all over the lands, and though I have since found parts of the answer myself, the ways of the world has me yet confused.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Since I am blessed with the fortune to meet thee in thy flesh, I thought I would—

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: If you've had your ideas, why ask me?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I wish merely to learn from thy explanation for my own betterment and to fill in the blanks... To tell the truth, the painting's true meaning eludes me still. Pray tell, wherefore was the end of the waterfall just one swift stroke, leaving naught but a swath of emptiness?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: —Crude mounts utmost risen. The scenery within the scroll extends endlessly. The waterfall soars into the skies, leaving naught but white. 'Tis a way to depict the great mountains and rivers undepictable within the scroll...

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Hrm... This is merely conjecture. I am hoping you could do away with the secrecy and reveal the truth. 'Tis making me blush.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Beauty, especially that of an art piece, is in the eye of the beholder. It falls on you to find your own interpretation.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Nonetheless... You racked your brains so for only that?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Much of what we do in life is seeking answers.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: If not for this matter gnawing at my mind, I would not have had the fortune to feast my eyes upon thy landscapes within the scrolls.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I suppose so.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Alas, the stroke you are asking was one that I began at whim and also one that I ended at whim. That's all.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: By the time I got to the waterfall, I no longer wanted to continue, and so I stopped there. I took a look afterwards and thought it was rather picturesque, so I gave it a name and sent it your master's way.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: —I could never have imagined!

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Disappointed?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Having spent such a long time in the painting, and you ended up with quite possibly the most boring answer—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Not at all. Leaving aside all that I have learned inside the scroll, thy answer is most interesting!

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Drawn on a whim, and stopped on a whim... I once thought that there is meaning to all things upon this world. As time passed, I became far too entrenched in my search, unable to pluck myself out.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Right, right. We need not be so focused on the meaning behind everything... If there is but one answer, to repeatedly scrutinize would merely be a futile exercise.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I had heard from my master an aphorism: 'Where there was naught at first, from whence could dust have emerged.' Mayhaps it means the same thing?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Everyone has their own interpretations. As long as you understand that, it's not necessarily a bad thing to be cocky.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oh, I shall keep that in mind. Many thanks.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: When I gave your master this piece, I told him merely three words, 'Crude Mounts Utmost.' The 'Risen' in its name... is his interpretation.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: 'Risen?'

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Do you know what your master saw in it?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: He gazed not upon its landscapes with thee?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: He didn't.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Hoh?!

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: A-Am I returning to the painting...?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oh, this must be what the head priest saw—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Is that... my head priest?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: He had scraped the soles of his feet, he was starving, and he walked three full days and nights of hunger.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: He prayed many times, as many as two thousand and a score, and yet he never thought a thing about his life and death. He merely felt sadness and lamented his inability to understand.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Did you save... my head priest?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I had already saved him once at the K'u-t'an River. I didn't help him this time.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Think about it. At his young age, he had already been through such hardships.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Think about how he went from that to the warm, caring head priest that you know.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: And how he added the word 'risen' to the painting's title.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Head Priest...

a.text: The lands he walked were filled with starvation.
All that he could see, hear, and tell were nothing but tragedy.
With each step, the young Higashi monk paused to recite the sutras.
Time passes like a flowing river, and this moment is everlasting.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: On the day I left the monastery, my head priest bestowed upon me my name, Saga.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: He had seen the coldness of mankind, yet he was never disheartened. Even the collapse of Mount Sky did not sway him.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: After the young wandering monk made his way back to Higashi, he decided to take in a group of children with nowhere to turn to. He built a monastery in the mountains, and that's how he became the head priest you often speak of.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: It's not that uncommon of a story.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: The crude mounts had not fallen... That was the meaning the head priest sought to give the painting.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Very well! Then, in his stead, I shall see all the sights there are to see in this vast world!

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Well, as you please.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Now that you got that weight off your shoulders, it's time for you to leave.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: W-Wait, master!

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: This is merely the original source of my perplexity. Having traveled the scrolls some ten years, I am afraid there are certain things I must ascertain for my worries to dissipate.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Ask away.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: But know that this is the last chance I'm giving you. I'm not fond of blabbering people.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: The inhabitants of the paintings. Are they real or not?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: That's an interesting question. You know they are from the painting. Why ask if they are real or not?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Oft did I nod off when we studied our scriptures, yet in my languidness I was able to constant seek out truth... For ten years have I walked the landscapes in thy painting, though I yet remain befuddled.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Pray tell, what is real?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: ...Real.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: When we look at those who are unreal in the painting, as those who are real, we are able to laugh off all the fake lives and deaths depicted therein.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: But if we are yet inhabitants of a painting, and we will one day vanish into the thin air, would you still be able to remain so calm?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: All men will one day cease to be. There is little reason to be tormented by that which is inevitable. By approaching all things from the heart and living my life naturally and freely, there is naught to fear.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Man is not necessarily free. Everything that I've drawn, be it real or otherwise, is merely my way of interrogating myself.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Man is naturally free.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Wrong. Both you and I are habitants of a painting.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You seek to solve this problem by yourself, yet you know not a thing about yourself. How do you mean to seek truth?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: In the end, what is real, and what is false? Are you sure you can truly tell them apart?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: And why take it so seriously?

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: So thou meanst... I am yet within the painting right this moment?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: ...You've truly left my scrolls, that I can assure you.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I'm only asking, how do you prove that these landscapes before your eyes are not yet another boring painting scroll?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: The roads you've trodden, the people you've met, their births and deaths, and their setbacks in life. All of these things might merely be events drawn at the whim of an artist without any particular meaning assigned.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: The so-called reality that you people spend an entire lifetime looking for is yet another fantasy.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: We are merely characters in a scroll. The viewers see the events that transpire in the painting and either applaud or criticize its contents.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Our lives are but a fantasy, like a dewdrop or lightning, leaving not a trace in the end.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Let's stop here. You're wasting both your time and mine, and it's getting on my nerves.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: I will find a chance to pluck the other ones out. You should get going.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: Lava came a long way solely for the chance to meet thee... yet thou wouldst not grant her an audience?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: That's none of your business.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You don't know why they came, so stay out of it.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: —Don't push your luck, Saga.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: One more word, and I'll have you truly regret it.

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: But I promised Lava to present this to thee, at the very least.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You—This...?!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Found you...!
